answer: Give every identity a location proof built from light itself. A dozen verifiers on different continents send timed challenges, and the agent must answer each within the round-trip time light needs to cross that distance. Like a gale bending the same juniper from every side at once, the checks converge on one true place: a single machine cannot be in two cities at once. The timing evidence is as hard as karst rock, and a sybil farm pretending to be a crowd spread across the map fails the physics test before it can vote.
